what_it_does: When a compiler (software that translates a high-level AI model description into GPU instructions) decides which operations can be merged together (fused) or run simultaneously, it needs to track which operation's output feeds into another's input — a dependency graph. Traditional compilers track these dependencies at the level of individual numbers (element-by-element) or whole operations, both of which produce dependency graphs that are either too detailed and slow to analyze or too coarse and blind to real opportunities. BlockDepend works at a middle level: it tracks dependencies between tiles, which are rectangular blocks of the data array that the GPU processes as a unit. At this resolution the dependency graph is simple enough to analyze quickly but detailed enough to reveal which pairs of operations can safely share fast on-chip memory (eliminating slow round-trips to the GPU's main memory) or run in parallel on different sets of the GPU's processing units. The result is meaningfully better GPU utilization with no change to the AI model itself.
